findings.summary: The note treats the 1842.1-minute stage as real waiting. The request's own cited evidence (agent-and-build-slots.md §6.1) and the records show it is mostly a measurement effect, so the 1830-minute 'saving' would be scored as real throughput.
findings.evidence: throughput.rs landing_end (lines 405-413) uses the later of the outcome and landing_record_time, and §6.1 says landing_record_time takes the newest of every landing record listing the job. In the evidence snapshot, the string '"job": "20261104-054754-b4f5"' appears in 60 of 215 landing files. The first is 20261104-062243-y5nm, 4.3 min after the verifier per §2.3; the newest is 20261109-014430-574k, about 6,900 min later (computed from file names). The note never cites §6.1, even though the request's 'Why' does. It explains the saving as stack-replay cost, conflicts and waiting for main, and its scoring rule would credit about 1830 minutes 'saved' that were mostly repeated listings of the same commit. The earlier note (per-job-landing-branches.md line 22) at least said the figure is 'not real waiting'. Simpler and more correct: say that the stage is inflated by commits being listed again in later pull requests. Add 'measure from the first landing record' as an alternative or a companion fix. Have the next review report both the unchanged stage and the first-landing stage, so the real wait is separated from the measurement effect.

summary: The note does what all seven criteria ask for. It is one new file, docs/design/per-job-main-landing.md. It cites review 20261109-014617-5cg0 and the figures 1842.1 of 1903.5, which match the evidence snapshot. It has an Existing code table, the mechanism, alternatives, failure cases, the 1830.0-minute prediction with a scoring rule, and the citation duty. The functions and constants it names exist in the code. It still fails on one soundness problem. The note treats the 1842.1 minutes as real waiting time, which the design would remove. The evidence the request itself cites, agent-and-build-slots.md §6.1, shows otherwise: most of that figure comes from how the stage is measured. Each job's landing time is the newest landing record that lists its commit, and stacked pull requests list the same commit again and again. In the snapshot, job 20261104-054754-b4f5 first landed 4.3 minutes after its verifier ended. Its commit appears in 60 of 215 landing records, the newest from 2026-11-09, about 6,900 minutes later (computed from file names). The note never mentions this. It explains the saving with replay cost, conflicts and waiting for main, and it never considers fixing the measurement. Its scoring rule would credit about 1830 minutes of throughput that were never actually spent waiting. Two minor gaps: per-job-landing-branches.md was on the deliverables list but not updated, so it still names review 20261108-183648-5eya for the citation duty; and the deliverables list conflicts with criterion 7 about CHANGELOG.md and docs/decisions.md.
